messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — kicking off a short thread to capture decisions for fan‑in / fan‑out handshake semantics for multi-step tool calls. Need product + infra alignment on API surface, defaults, and launch gates. @Maria PTAL

Maria Lopez: Confirmed customer ask from FinOps pilot: deterministic ordering for some tool chains (ledger writes), clear retry budget, and visibility into partial failures. They can accept best-effort fan‑out for non-critical steps.

Jamal Singh: Infra note — risks: bursty parallel calls will blow up connection pools and KV cache churn. Requirement: per-tool timeouts + global saga timeout; also per-tool circuit breaker + retry budget.

Kim Park: Proposed API sketch (MVP): server-driven aggregator that returns a saga id and streams partial results with correlation ids. Example request: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "input": "Prepare invoice and charge card",
  "tool_calls": [
    {"id":"fetch_user","tool":"user-service.get","mode":"parallel"},
    {"id":"pricing","tool":"pricing-service.calc","mode":"parallel"},
    {"id":"charge","tool":"payments.charge","mode":"sequential","after":["fetch_user","pricing"]}
  ],
  "saga_timeout_ms": 30000,
  "defaults": {"per_tool_timeout_ms": 5000, "retry_policy": "exponential:2"},
  "best_effort": false
}
```
Server responses: stream of partial objects like `{saga_id, call_id, status, payload, attempt}` and final aggregated summary.

Alex Chen: MVP scope suggestion: - fan‑out up to 5 concurrent tool calls - per-tool timeout & retry (max 2 retries) - streaming partials + final aggregation - idempotency_key per tool_call - an explicit `strict_order` flag for chains that must be sequential (finance). No distributed transaction guarantees in MVP.

Maria Lopez: Customer launch criteria: SDK examples (JS/Python), docs with the request/response patterns, one external canary with finance pilot, telemetry surfaced in Console (per-call latency, cost, success/partial), and clear error codes for partial success.

Jamal Singh: Ops launch checklist: rate limit per-saga, global concurrency cap, per-tool circuit breakers, traceable correlation IDs (saga_id + call_id), logging of retry_count and final outcome. Metrics required: saga_success_rate, partial_success_rate, avg_aggregate_latency, per_tool_error_rate.

Kim Park: Edge-case decisions: - duplicate suppression: require `idempotency_key` per tool_call; server must de‑duplicate within a 24h window. - client-visible retry_count included in final aggregation so callers can adapt. - if `best_effort=true`, return partial success with non-2xx top-level code but structured detail for each call.

Alex Chen: Decision ask — proceed with MVP as proposed? If yes, product will draft acceptance criteria and examples; infra will spec rate limits and circuit breakers; devex will draft SDK ergonomics for streaming partials.

Maria Lopez: +1 :thumbsup: Add `strict_order=true` for transactional sequences and require explicit opt‑in.

Jamal Singh: +1. We'll spec defaults: saga_timeout_ms=30000, per_tool_timeout_ms=5000, max_parallel_calls=5, retry_policy=max_retries=2.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for feature/parallel-tool-calls on staging at 2026-04-01T09:00Z

Alex Chen: Great — I'll push a short PR with the API examples + acceptance checklist today and tag everyone for review.
